claim: An argument map exposes the warrant and its qualification instead of asserting a cause

input.position: automatic scoring can replace one of two human raters
evidence: machine to human quadratic weighted kappa 0.79 on 240 double-scored essays
human to human quadratic weighted kappa 0.81 on the same 240 essays

map.claim: Automatic scoring may substitute for one rater in a two-rater design for this essay type.
evidence: machine to human agreement reached 0.79 on 240 double-scored essays
human to human agreement reached 0.81 on the same essays
map.warrant: A substitute rater is acceptable when its agreement with a human rater is close to the agreement between two humans on the same material.
map.qualification: The comparison holds for the 240 essays of this single prompt type and does not extend to other prompts or grade levels.
map.counterposition: Comparable agreement does not show that the two raters fail in the same places, so a shared blind spot remains possible.

claim: Supplied sources are compared on a shared dimension, and absence of evidence is reported as absence

output.dimension: prompt genre rather than language family
output.convergence: Tran (2021) reports 0.79 and Silva (2023) reports 0.83 on argumentative prompts.
output.tension: Ito (2022) reports 0.74 on narrative prompts, which is lower than either argumentative result.
output.absence: No supplied source reports agreement for expository prompts, so the pattern cannot be extended to that genre.

claim: Shortening preserves the hedge, the quantity, and the scope statement

input.text: In this study, which was conducted over the course of a single academic semester, we set out to examine the extent to which an automatic scoring procedure may be able to approximate the judgements of trained human raters. Our analysis, which was based on a set of 240 essays that had been double scored, indicates that agreement may reach 0.79, although it should be noted that this figure applies only to the argumentative prompt that was used in the present study.

output.text: On 240 double-scored essays, agreement between automatic and human scores may reach 0.79 for the argumentative prompt used here.
